title: Chevron stripe jumper
excerpt: A drop-shoulder jumper in dk yarn worked in a chevron stripe pattern. Regular increases and decreases bend horizontal stripes into a zigzag across the front and back. Graded XS to 3XL.
sourceNotes: Chevron stripe jumpers in dk weight are a popular beginner ripple-stitch garment project.

glossaryTerms.definition: A row in which groups of dc are increased at peaks and decreased at troughs at regular intervals. The same stitch count is maintained across every row; the increases and decreases simply redistribute stitches to create the zigzag shape.

Double crochet two together: insert the hook, pull up a loop, then insert the hook in the next stitch, pull up a loop, and draw through all three loops. Used at the trough points in the chevron to pull the fabric inward.

crochet.gaugeText: 18 dc x 20 rows = 10 x 10 cm in dk on a 4 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Graded XS to 3XL. Size M: 104.4 cm bust.

content.text: on row 1: work 2 dc into the peak stitch, dc across the valley,

at the trough, then continue. The repeat is 12 stitches wide. Keep the stitch count the same every row. Switch colour every 4 rows to build the stripe sequence. The chevron peaks and troughs align automatically when each row follows the same increase-decrease sequence.
Size M: 188 sts wide, 81.7 cm body. Sleeve 63.3 cm.
Chain 190. Establish chevron repeat. Work in 4-row stripes for 81.7 cm. Shape neck on front. Seam shoulders.
Chain 72. Work plain dc stripes, increasing each end every 4 rows for 63.3 cm.
Seam sides. Work 2 rounds dc around neck in colour A.
The fair-isle-style yoke pullover uses surface colourwork in rounds to place a patterned band across the shoulders.
